path_decisions.rationale: Stop-loss ATR multiplier defaults are inconsistent across strategies (2.0 trend, 1.5 elliott, none for mean_rev/momentum/funding) — edge case testing needed to find which combos fail in backtest

profit_target_exit() only handles LONG positions (close >= target_price) — SHORT entries never trigger profit exit, creating systematic loss capture failure for mean_reversion short entries and volatility_breakout short entries

Trailing stops in trend_following and volatility_breaking use ATR-based highest-since-entry but reset highest on ANY exit (including profit_target) — premature trailing stop re-entry creates false exit signals that reduce win rate

RSI-adaptive profit targets in trend_following use global mean of ALL entry RSI values instead of per-entry RSI — this makes the adaptive mechanism effectively static after initial calibration, defeating its purpose

evidence: quantflow/strategy/templates/_runtime.py:167 — target_price = entry_price * (1.0 + profit_take_pct) — LONG-only profit target, no SHORT path
quantflow/strategy/templates/_runtime.py:169 — if float(close.iloc[i]) >= target_price — condition only met when price RISES, never for SHORT positions where price must FALL
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:50 — self._atr_multiplier = p.get('atr_multiplier', 2.0) — default 2.0 for ATR cap filter, not calibrated as stop-loss multiplier
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:56 — self._trailing_stop_atr_mult: float = p.get('trailing_stop_atr_mult', 3.0) — trailing multiplier 3.0 may be too wide for BTC/USDT 1d
quantflow/strategy/templates/volatility_breakout.py:51 — self._trailing_stop_atr_mult: float = p.get('trailing_stop_atr_mult', 2.5) — 2.5 ATR trailing for 4h volatility breakout, may exit too early
quantflow/strategy/templates/mean_reversion.py:39 — self._min_conditions: int = p.get('min_conditions', 2) — no trailing stop, no ATR stop at all for mean reversion
quantflow/strategy/templates/elliott_wave.py:27 — self.atr_stop_mult = self.params.get('atr_stop_mult', 1.5) — declared but never used in generate_signals or on_bar
quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:257-267 — RSI-adaptive uses avg_entry_rsi = float(rsi_at_entry.mean()) — global average over ALL entries, not per-entry RSI

quantflow/strategy/templates/trend_following.py:283-292 — trailing stop resets highest when exits or profit_exits fire, but profit_target_exit fires on SHORT entries too (wrong direction), causing highest corruption
quantflow/strategy/templates/volatility_breakout.py:370-372 — entries combined (long_count | short_count) into single entries series — profit_target_exit then treats all as LONG entries
quantflow/signal/generator.py:69 — hit_rates default 0.5 for unknown strategies — new/low-sample strategies get equal weight, diluting high-performer signals
quantflow/signal/risk_engine.py:106-107 — strategy_exposure sums ALL positions regardless of strategy_id — _check_strategy_budget sums total portfolio not per-strategy

candidate_solution.summary: 6 critical bottlenecks limiting win rate to 65%+: profit_target_exit LONG-only bug, per-strategy budget aggregation error, RSI-adaptive global-vs-per-entry flaw, ATR stop multiplier misalignment across strategies, trailing stop premature reset interaction, and missing regime detection module

bottlenecks.title: profit_target_exit LONG-only — SHORT positions never profit-exit
bottlenecks.detail: profit_target_exit() checks close >= entry_price * (1 + pct) exclusively. When mean_reversion or volatility_breakout enters SHORT, the function records the entry but can never trigger profit because price must go UP to hit target. SHORT positions can only exit via max_holding_bars timeout — turning what should be profitable shorts into forced time-bar exits at potentially worse prices. This systematically reduces win rate for ALL strategies that enter short (mean_reversion, volatility_breakout, funding_rate).
bottlenecks.fix: Add direction tracking: if short position, target_price = entry_price * (1 - profit_take_pct) and check close <= target_price

bottlenecks.title: volatility_breakout entries mix LONG+SHORT into single series — profit_target_exit misinterprets
bottlenecks.detail: entries = (long_count >= min) | (short_count >= min) merges long+short entries into one boolean series. profit_target_exit then treats all entries as LONG. A short entry at bb_lower will have its target computed as entry_price * 1.05 — a price it should FALL from, making the target unreachable.
bottlenecks.fix: Separate entries into long_entries / short_entries series, call profit_target_exit for each with direction-aware logic

bottlenecks.title: RSI-adaptive profit targets use global mean instead of per-entry RSI
bottlenecks.detail: Line 261-266: rsi_at_entry = rsi[entries]; avg_entry_rsi = float(rsi_at_entry.mean()). This averages RSI across ALL historical entries then applies a single discount/premium. With 100+ entries over a backtest, the average converges to ~50, making the 0.8x/1.2x adjustment effectively useless. Should be per-entry: check RSI at each individual entry point.
bottlenecks.fix: Move RSI-adaptive logic inside profit_target_exit or compute per-entry effective_pct in the generate_signals loop

bottlenecks.title: ATR stop multiplier misalignment — elliott_wave declares atr_stop_mult but never uses it
bottlenecks.detail: self.atr_stop_mult = 1.5 is initialized but never referenced in generate_signals or on_bar. ElliottWaveStrategy has no ATR-based stop loss at all. Similarly, mean_reversion, momentum_rotation, and funding_rate have NO ATR stops — they rely only on profit_target_exit (which is LONG-only per B1) and max_holding_bars. Without volatility-adaptive stops, these strategies are blind to market regime changes.
bottlenecks.fix: Wire atr_stop_mult into elliott_wave generate_signals; add trailing_stop or ATR stop to mean_reversion, momentum_rotation, funding_rate

bottlenecks.title: Trailing stop + profit_target interaction corrupts highest-since-entry tracking
bottlenecks.detail: The trailing stop loop tracks highest close since entry. When profit_target_exit fires (line 288: if exits.iloc[i] or profit_exits.iloc[i]: in_pos = False), the highest tracking resets. But due to B1, profit_target_exit fires incorrectly on SHORT entries, resetting in_pos prematurely. Additionally, when a legitimate profit target fires mid-trend, re-entry is not tracked — the trailing stop mechanism has no concept of re-entry after partial exit.
bottlenecks.fix: Separate entry direction tracking; add re-entry logic or make trailing stop track per-trade rather than per-entry-signal

bottlenecks.title: strategy_budget check sums ALL positions regardless of strategy_id
bottlenecks.detail: _check_strategy_budget iterates portfolio.positions.values() and sums exposure for ALL positions, not filtering by signal.strategy_id. The budget check computes total portfolio exposure vs total_value * budget_pct, not per-strategy exposure. This means if trend_following has 15% budget but mean_reversion also has 15%, and both have positions, the check sums both against EACH strategy's budget — making the budget more restrictive than intended.
bottlenecks.fix: Filter positions by matching strategy_id metadata: need position.strategy_id field or position_tag tracking

bottlenecks.title: No regime detection module — all strategies trade identically in trending/ranging/volatile markets
bottlenecks.detail: None of the 6 strategy templates check market regime (trending vs ranging vs volatile). trend_following enters even in flat markets; mean_reversion enters even in strong trends. Top quant systems use ATR regime filters (e.g., ADX > 25 for trend, ADX < 20 for range) to gate entries. Without this, trend strategies accumulate losses in sideways markets and mean-reversion strategies get run over in trends.
bottlenecks.fix: Add regime_detection module to L2 indicators; wire regime filter into strategy entry conditions

parameter_gaps.rationale: 3.0 ATR trailing is too wide — allows 9-12% drawdown from peak in a single ATR period before exit. Most profitable trades in BTC close within 2 ATR of peak.
Volatility breakouts are fast-moving — 2.5 ATR on 4h gives too much room for the move to reverse before exit.

3% profit target on a mean-reversion trade that entered at BB lower band is often too aggressive — price needs to cross the entire band width to hit target. 2% is more achievable, increasing win rate.
Mean reversion on 4h timeframe gives only 40 hours — many BB-lower entries need 3-5 days to revert. 15-25 bars (60-100h) better captures the reversion.

2.0x ATR cap filter is too restrictive — it rejects entries when volatility is above average, but trending moves ARE volatile. Lowering to 1.5 allows trend entries during the volatility expansion that accompanies trends.

notes: The profit_target_exit LONG-only bug (B1+B2) is the single highest-impact bottleneck. It means that for every strategy that enters SHORT (mean_reversion short, volatility_breakout short, funding_rate short), the profit target exit can NEVER fire. These trades exit ONLY via max_holding_bars timeout, which is essentially a forced exit at arbitrary price. This alone could account for 5-10% of potential win rate being left on the table. The RSI-adaptive bug (B3) is second — it makes a carefully implemented feature effectively dead code.
